nodes.label: CyberAlchemy
nodes.plain_language: The parent Product that People and Teams supports.
nodes.claim: A source-bound parent Product projection anchors this subproduct without redefining CyberAlchemy.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not owned or redefined by People and Teams.

nodes.label: People and Teams
nodes.plain_language: The CyberAlchemy subproduct that makes human and collective collaboration meaning explicit.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy needs a private product boundary for Person, Team, membership, role, and responsibility meaning.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a directory, HR system, identity provider, authorization service, or organization chart.

nodes.label: Explicit Human Collaboration Meaning
nodes.plain_language: Model people and teams without turning collaboration facts into identity, privacy, or authority overreach.
nodes.claim: Stable identities plus explicit membership, roles, and responsibilities can reduce collaboration ambiguity while preserving human and authority boundaries.

source_refs.selector: A Person is one human individual

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not product proof, market evidence, implementation, or permission to process personal data.

nodes.label: Model People and Teams
nodes.plain_language: Let CyberAlchemy refer to Persons and Teams through explicit, reviewable collaboration relations.
nodes.claim: The Product should preserve Person, Team, membership, role, and responsibility meaning without inferring authority.

source_refs.selector: A Product Capability is a stable

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an adopted capability, runtime, component, identity system, or authorization system.

nodes.label: Person
nodes.plain_language: One human individual participating in CyberAlchemy work.
nodes.claim: Person identity is stable across accounts, roles, Teams, Projects, and sessions.

source_refs.selector: A Person is one human individual

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus the owner of each bounded Person reference
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an account, credential, role, permission, record, agent, or authority envelope.

nodes.label: Team
nodes.plain_language: A named collective of Persons coordinating toward one purpose.
nodes.claim: Team identity remains distinct from its current member set, roles, responsibilities, Projects, and access groups.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus each Team owner route
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a Project, organization, department, chat channel, access group, role, or authority envelope.

nodes.label: Team Membership
nodes.plain_language: One explicit Person-to-Team participation record with its own lifecycle.
nodes.claim: Membership binds exactly one Person and one Team and implies no role, responsibility, permission, or authority.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner plus the affected Person and Team owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not employment, ownership, a role, a permission, or an access-group entry.

nodes.label: Team Role
nodes.plain_language: A named participation expectation inside one Team.
nodes.claim: A Team Role may be assigned through membership but never grants authority by itself.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner plus the Team owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a permission, job title, owner route, identity, policy, or authority grant.

nodes.label: Responsibility
nodes.plain_language: A bounded expected outcome or duty owned by one Person or Team.
nodes.claim: Responsibility identifies the responsible party and challenge route without granting execution or decision authority.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner plus the responsibility owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not permission, authority, task completion, conformance, or employment duty.

nodes.label: People and Teams Declaration Contract
nodes.plain_language: A bounded declaration of Person, Team, membership, role, or responsibility meaning and its owner references.
nodes.claim: Every declaration must identify its concept kind, owner route, intended use, source, lifecycle posture, and privacy boundary.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an instance admission, authority envelope, consent record, or implementation command.

nodes.label: People and Teams Model Contract
nodes.plain_language: A closed candidate graph of explicit collaboration meaning and unresolved residue.
nodes.claim: The output preserves identities, typed relations, source references, gaps, and a no-authority ceiling.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a Person directory, Team registry of fact, accepted design, system ontology, or runtime output.

nodes.label: People Privacy Minimization
nodes.plain_language: Use only the minimum Person attributes required by one declared consumer and purpose.
nodes.claim: A Person reference does not permit private-attribute inference or unnecessary data collection.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus the applicable privacy and data owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not consent, legal basis, identity verification, retention authority, or a universal privacy policy.

nodes.label: Person Identity Does Not Collapse
nodes.plain_language: Keep the human separate from every account, role, record, and participation relation.
nodes.claim: No account, role, membership, ownership, or observation may replace Person identity.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus People and Teams ontology owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not identity verification or a universal identity model.

nodes.label: Membership Must Be Explicit
nodes.plain_language: Represent every Person-to-Team participation through one lifecycle record.
nodes.claim: A channel, repository, account group, or role list cannot silently establish Team membership.

source_refs.selector: Add Persons through explicit Team Membership

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner plus Team owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an access-control group or automatic membership inference.

nodes.label: Role Is Not Authority
nodes.plain_language: A participation role does not grant permission or decision authority.
nodes.claim: Any authority effect requires a separately owned authority record.

source_refs.selector: membership alone never implies a role, responsibility, or

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner plus authority owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an authority policy, permission mapper, or authorization decision.

nodes.label: Responsibility Must Name Its Owner
nodes.plain_language: Every responsibility names its responsible Person or Team and challenge route.
nodes.claim: Unowned or multiply ambiguous responsibilities remain residue rather than being inferred.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams ontology owner plus responsibility owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not task completion, authority, permission, or automatic accountability proof.

nodes.label: Personal Data Has A Bounded Use
nodes.plain_language: Do not collect or infer Person attributes without a declared need and owner.
nodes.claim: Every modeled personal attribute must be necessary for one named consumer and use or remain absent.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus applicable privacy and data owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not consent, legal advice, retention approval, or permission to process data.

nodes.label: Legible Collaboration
nodes.plain_language: People can see who and which Team a collaboration statement refers to without confusing identities and roles.
nodes.claim: Closed references and non-collapse rules reduce ambiguous ownership and handoffs.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not proof of correct understanding, adoption, or realized product value.

nodes.label: Auditable Membership
nodes.plain_language: Join, leave, and role changes remain historically visible instead of overwriting participation.
nodes.claim: Membership lifecycle evidence can later support continuity and challenge without becoming authority.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams product owner plus Team owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not employment history, access audit, runtime evidence, or conformance proof.

nodes.label: Unresolved Person References
nodes.plain_language: Count Person references that cannot resolve to one bounded identity or named gap.
nodes.claim: Fewer unresolved references may indicate more legible collaboration, subject to consumer review.
nodes.owner_route: Future People and Teams evidence owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not identity truth, product value proof, or authorization evidence.

nodes.label: Orphan Responsibilities
nodes.plain_language: Count responsibilities without one resolvable responsible Person or Team and challenge route.
nodes.claim: Orphan count exposes missing collaboration ownership without inventing an owner.
nodes.owner_route: Future People and Teams evidence owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not proof that responsibility was accepted, fulfilled, or authorized.
